items.title: NASA Science
items.summary: What color is the Moon? It depends on the night -- and the time. Outside of the Earth's atmosphere, the dark Moon, which shines by reflected sunlight, appears a magnificently brown-tinged gray. The featured image highlights a collection of apparent colors of the full moon on Earth, documented by one astrophotographer over 10 years from different locations across Italy. A red- or yellow-colored moon usually indicates a moon seen near the horizon. There, some of the blue light has been scattered away by a long path through the Earth's atmosphere, sometimes laden with fine dust. A blue-colored moon is more rare and can indicate an atmosphere carrying larger dust particles.

items.title: Prognostic value of the preoperative C-reactive protein-to-lymphocyte ratio in patients with non-metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma
items.summary: by Minchao Qin, Zhongwen Feng, Chao Zhang, Wei Song, Kai Wang, Zhen Chen Background Systemic inflammation is associated with the prognosis of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). The C-reactive protein-to-lymphocyte ratio (CLR) combines systemic inflammation and host immune status. However, its prognostic value in non-metastatic ccRCC remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between preoperative CLR and survival outcomes in patients with non-metastatic ccRCC. Methods We retrospectively included 414 patients with non-metastatic ccRCC who underwent partial or radical nephrectomy. The primary Cox analyses treated ln(CLR) as a continuous variable and assessed overall survival (OS) and the cause-specific hazard of ccRCC-related death.
items.author: Minchao Qin, Zhongwen Feng, Chao Zhang et al.

items.title: Development of a competency framework for public health nurses in China: A modified Delphi study
items.summary: by Chunxia He, Lingli Yan, Jia Yin, Qian Yao, Jiali Zhang, Jimei Zhang, Xiuying Hu Background Public health nurses play a pivotal role in primary public health services, yet China lacks a systematic, context-specific competency framework to support workforce development. This study aimed to develop a competency framework for public health nurses in China to guide capacity-building initiatives. Methods A preliminary competency framework was constructed based on a literature review, job analysis, and semi-structured interviews with 22 frontline practitioners and comprised six domains, 16 subdomains, and 52 competencies. A two-round Delphi survey was then conducted with 21 experts from multiple regions with expertise in community nursing, public health, primary care medicine, and nursing education and related specialties.

items.title: Detection of potentially curable recurrence after colorectal cancer surgery in a real-world population
items.summary: by Ivonne J. H. Schoenaker, Richard M. Brohet, Evelyn J. Finnema, Dominique C. Damminga, Helle-Brit Fiebrich, Wouter H. de Vos tot Nederveen Cappel, Henderik L. van Westreenen Introduction After curative surgery for colorectal cancer (CRC), patients undergo surveillance because of the risk of recurrence; however, only a subset develops recurrence amenable to further curative-intent treatment. The primary aim of follow‑up is to identify patients with potentially curable recurrence. Materials and methods A retrospective analysis was performed of stage I–IV CRC patients who underwent curative-intent treatment and entered postoperative surveillance at Isala between 2014 and 2018. Follow‑up was conducted according to Dutch guideline‑based protocols for 60 months.
items.author: Ivonne J. H. Schoenaker, Richard M. Brohet, Evelyn J. Finnema et al.

items.title: Age-specific income losses due to HPV-attributable cancers in Singapore
items.summary: by Robin Blythe, Nicholas Graves, N. Gopalakrishna Iyer, Marco A. Peres Introduction The link between Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and cancer is well-established. In Singapore, bivalent HPV vaccines are subsidised for females, but not males. Economic analysis of HPV vaccination has generally assessed the costs to the health system, but this may not be as relevant to individual decision-making as potential lost income. We estimated the impact of bivalent HPV 16/18 vaccination on sick leave, unemployment, and premature mortality as a function of age and sex to understand the broader impact of HPV-related cancers. Methods We developed a population-level economic model to estimate lifetime income losses by diagnosis age, sex and cancer type.

items.summary: by Jui-Kun Chiang, Po-Chen Chiang, Malcolm Koo Electronic health record-based oncology studies depend on computable case definitions, but different operational definitions may identify different patient populations and change downstream estimates. Female patients aged 20 years or older were identified after a 12-month washout period and exclusion of patients with carcinoma in situ only. Pairwise one-to-one propensity-score matching was performed using 13 baseline covariates.

items.title: Hudson River Estuary sediments contain high fractional abundances of preserved globothalamean foraminiferal organic linings at Piermont, New York
items.summary: by Logan Brenner, Laura Haynes, Batoul Saad, Maisie Klem, Amelia Lang, Elizabeth Grey Linsley, William Riley, Sophie Spink, Carolyn Zhao, Margie Turrin, Lorelei Curtin Foundational to an estuarine ecosystem is the composition of its sediments, with benthic foraminifera serving as a key component. While it is common to find intact and deformed tests, foraminiferal organic linings (FOLs; foraminifera whose tests dissolved) are not always present in sediment samples. Identifying where FOLs are preserved is a necessary first step towards determining what promotes their development and burial. Here we document the prevalence of globothalamean FOLs in the Hudson River Estuary (HRE) at the Pier in Piermont, New York, USA.

items.title: Alcohol use and its associations with mental health across the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic
items.summary: by Lu Zhang, Bianca Ton, Louise Mewton, Susanne Schweizer Background While the COVID-19 pandemic caused major disruptions to social connections and lifestyles, many countries continued the sale of alcohol as an essential commodity. Evidence on change in alcohol use, and its association with mental health and wellbeing during the pandemic is, however, mixed and limited to initial periods of the pandemic. This study aimed to address these research gaps. Methods Data were drawn from the COVID-19 Risks Across the Lifespan (CORAL) Study, a three-wave longitudinal study conducted between May 2020 and April 2021. The present sample included 2,369 participants (age M = 38.81 ± 16.94 years, range = 11–100; 90% females) from the United Kingdom, United States, and Australia.

items.title: Testing hardware quantum machine learning claims with a null circuit: fill prediction on Binance futures with 129 qubits of an IBM Heron processor
items.summary: Quantum processors are now used as feature generators for classical models on tabular data. A circuit encodes each record, the device returns expectation values, and a classical model learns from them. A recent report claimed large gains from such features, gains that appeared only on noisy hardware. These claims are hard to check, because a quantum device is not a static function. Its state changes from job to job and from one calibration to the next, and that drift can leak information about the outcome into the features. We propose a five-step protocol for testing claims of this kind. It runs a circuit that carries no data in the same jobs as the real one.
items.author: Muhammad Faryad

items.title: The Effect of Large Apertures on Atmospheric Noise Spectra for Millimeter-wave Telescopes
items.summary: Ground-based millimeter and submillimeter telescopes produce astronomical maps that contain a combination of noise inherent to themselves as well as contamination from foregrounds, with the strongest foreground being fluctuating atmospheric emission. While the emission of the turbulent atmosphere itself follows a scale-free power law, the atmosphere as seen by the telescope is modified by the properties of the instrument optics. A naive power-law extrapolation of the atmospheric noise spectrum ignores the blurring effect of the near-field beam, which becomes more pronounced for larger telescope apertures and at higher multipoles. In this work, we use a toy model to derive a semianalytic estimate of the atmospheric noise spectrum that takes into account the effects of near-field optics.
items.author: Thomas W. Morris, Neelima Sehgal

items.title: Longitudinal electric corner modes in continuum quantum gauge theory with matter
items.summary: Subregions in gauge theories give rise to edge modes and corner charges supported on their boundaries. While this is well-established classically and in quantum lattice gauge theories, the fate of corner modes remains poorly understood in continuum quantum field theories owing to their distributional nature. In this paper, we revisit this challenge and propose a new corner operator for a regional Cauchy slice algebra generated by local gauge-invariant observables of scalar QED in Minkowski spacetime. The corner mode is given by the longitudinal electric field sourced by the matter outside the subregion and thus constitutes a centre for the regional algebra.
items.author: Goncalo Araujo-Regado, Philipp A. Hoehn, Alok Laddha et al.

items.title: Quantum Advantage in Beam-Displacement Estimation for Inter-Satellite Quantum-Secure Time Transfer
items.summary: In this work, we investigate the practical feasibility of achieving a quantum advantage, in the context of inter-satellite quantum communication, of satellite position estimation. The investigation focuses on a quantum-enhanced scheme in which squeezing is added to the derivative mode of a Gaussian probe beam as a means of estimating photon-beam displacement. The performance of the scheme is compared against the standard quantum limit achieved by an optimal classical beam-displacement estimation scheme under a fair same-total-energy constraint. We find that although the benefit provided by squeezing rapidly diminishes as the inter-satellite distance increases due to diffraction-induced beam spreading and subsequent truncation by the finite receiver aperture, a quantum advantage can still be expected over inter-satellite distances up to approximately 100 km under practical satellite configurations.
items.author: Ziqing Wang, Robert Malaney

items.title: Biorthogonal universal quantum control
items.summary: As a paradigm for describing open-quantum-system dynamics, the non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation generally modifies state norms, complicating coherent control over the system's Hilbert space. With a general instantaneous frame spanned by biorthogonal ancillary bases, we develop a biorthogonal quantum-control theory for discrete-variable systems governed by time-dependent non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. In particular, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for extracting the transitionless pathways that transport parallel in ket and bra states. When this condition is satisfied by a set of projectors constructed with biorthogonal basis states, the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian becomes diagonal in the relevant biorthogonal subspace, enabling arbitrary initial state to evolve as a superposition of controlled transitionless passages.
items.author: Chen-yi Zhang, Jun Jing

items.title: Anomalous superradiant phases in a quantum Rabi zigzag chain under a synthetic gauge field
items.summary: We present the phase diagram of a one-dimensional quantum Rabi zigzag chain under an artificial gauge field, which is implemented via phase-modulated next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) hopping. For a system size of $N=8$, we analytically determine the order parameters and critical thresholds, identifying five distinct superradiant phases. For strong nearest-neighbor (NN) coupling, the system exhibits either a ferro-superradiant (FSR) or an antiferro-superradiant (AFSR) phase depending on its sign. Increasing NNN coupling induces a stripe antiferro-superradiant (sAFSR) phase with antiparallel NNN and parallel NN displacements, which is distinct from the conventional AFSR phase. Tuning the magnetic flux drives the system into chiral or antichiral superradiant phases with opposite ground-state photon currents, which are different from the conventional superradiant phases.
items.author: Jun-Bo Tang, Lin-Jun Li, Bin Wei et al.

items.title: Quantum query complexity of Hurwitz stability testing
items.summary: Determining whether every trajectory of the linear system $\dot{x}=Ax$ converges to zero (or, equivalently, whether $A$ is Hurwitz stable) is a fundamental problem in control theory. It arises, for example, in verifying the stability of feedback controllers and state observers, as well as of linearized dynamical models. We study the quantum query complexity of deciding whether a matrix $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ is Hurwitz stable, given an exact normalized block-encoding of $A$. The query complexity is characterized in terms of the system dimension $n$ and a supplied lower bound $0<ν\leq ω_A$ on the imaginary-axis distance $ω_A:=\min_{t\in\mathbb{R}}σ_{\min}(A-\mathrm{i}tI)$, where $σ_{\min}(A)$ is the smallest singular value of $A$.
items.author: Maxwell Fitzsimmons, Mohamed Serry, Meenu Kumari et al.

items.title: Encoded reversible addition in constant Toffoli depth
items.summary: We show that reversible in-place quantum addition modulo $2^n-1$ can be implemented in constant Toffoli depth using $O(n)$ space, provided that the variables are encoded in a certain non-standard form. Using measurement-based uncomputation, the Toffoli depth can be reduced to one. We also present space-depth tradeoffs and an application to programmable rotations.
items.author: Aidan Epperly, Isaac H. Kim, Mingyu Lee

items.title: MHC-II deficiency in a large Algerian cohort: Clinical, immunological, and genetic characterization.
items.summary: MHC class II (MHC-II) deficiency is a rare inborn error of immunity caused by defects in transcriptional regulators of MHC-II expression. In this study, we characterized the clinical, immunological, and molecular features of 107 patients from 98 unrelated Algerian families. Median ages at symptom onset and diagnosis were 5 and 14 mo, respectively, with pneumonia (82%) and chronic diarrhea (73%) predominating. CD4+ T cell lymphopenia occurred in 87.6% and naïve CD4+ T cell depletion in 86.0%. Among 99 genetically characterized patients, variants were identified exclusively in RFXANK (77.8%) and RFXAP (22.2%), including two predominant mutations (RFXANK c.338-25_338del and RFXAP c.368del) and four novel variants.

items.title: Combined Nav1.7-Nav1.8 channel abrogation: Supralinear suppression of excitability in a subpopulation of peripheral sensory neurons.
items.summary: There is a pressing need for nonaddictive pain therapeutics. Despite the genetic validation of peripheral voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channels as targets for non-opioid pain therapy, isoform-selective inhibition of Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 has yielded limited efficacy in clinical studies, with Nav1.8 blockade providing statistically significant but only partial pain relief. This raises the question: if block of Nav1.8 relieves pain only partially, what is needed for better pain relief? In this study, we utilized dynamic clamp, which permits precisely calibrated functional addition or subtraction of the current from any given channel, to systematically interrogate the combinatorial landscape of multiplex abrogation of currents from Nav1.7 and Nav1.8, both major contributors to electrogenesis within dorsal root ganglion neurons.

items.title: Nanobiomechanics in Oncology: Atomic Force Microscopy for Cancer Mechanophenotyping Using Cellular Young's Modulus.
items.summary: This review examines the current literature on the application of atomic force microscopy (AFM) to cancer mechanophenotyping, with particular emphasis on cellular Young's modulus and its potential diagnostic significance. A structured electronic search of PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar was conducted to identify studies published between 1999 and 2025 reporting AFM-based measurements of cellular Young's modulus in cancer-related models. Across multiple malignancies, reduced cellular stiffness is frequently observed in malignant compared with non-malignant cells and is associated with cytoskeletal remodelling, increased deformability and altered cell-matrix interactions. However, the relationship between Young's modulus and malignancy is not universally monotonic. Nanomechanical properties may vary across different pathological states and malignant phenotypes rather than following a simple monotonic trajectory, while invasive and metastatic cells can dynamically remodel their cytoskeleton and modify their stiffness in response to environmental and mechanical constraints.

items.title: Epstein-Barr Virus Serologic Profiles in Multiple Sclerosis and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease.
items.summary: Background and objectives Although the link between Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and multiple sclerosis (MS) is well established, geographic variation in EBV epidemiology warrants region-specific data from Asian populations. Beyond MS, the role of EBV in myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) remains far less studied. This study aimed to compare EBV serostatus and antibody titers in patients with MS, MOGAD, and controls in a Korean cohort. Methods We analyzed MS (n = 130), MOGAD (n = 125), and untreated tumor controls without known EBV association (n = 132). MS and controls were frequency-matched to MOGAD by age at sampling. Serum Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1) IgG, viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgG, VCA IgM, and early antigen (EA) IgG were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassays (LIAISON, DiaSorin).
items.author: Kang YR, Kim KH, Heo N, Min JH, Kim W, Kim SW, Shin HY, Huh SY, Hyun JW, Kim SH, Nam TS, Kim HJ.

items.title: Genetic Variation Underlying CSF Natural Killer T-Cell Frequency in Inflammatory CNS Diseases: A Genome-Wide Association Study.
items.summary: Background and objectives Natural killer T (NKT) cells bridge innate and adaptive immunity and are implicated in immune regulation in autoimmune diseases. In multiple sclerosis (MS), reduced CSF frequencies of NKT cells have been reported, but their role in disease pathogenesis remains unclear. Here, we investigated the genetic architecture underlying CSF NKT cell frequency variability in individuals with MS and other CNS diseases. Methods We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of CSF NKT cell frequencies in 456 individuals with MS, with replication in an independent cohort of 90 individuals with MS or other inflammatory CNS diseases. Functional follow-up assessed effects of the lead variant on integrin subunit beta 5 ( ITGB5) gene expression in CSF CD4 + T cells, and Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was used to evaluate causality.
